lines.say: Why do Jewish families light candles for eight nights in a row? It starts with a jar of oil.
More than two thousand years ago, the Temple in Jerusalem was taken over.
A small group called the Maccabees won it back, and wanted to light the Temple's lamp again.
But they found only enough pure oil for one day. And the story says it burned for eight days!
So on Hanukkah, families light one more candle each night. The extra candle in the middle is the helper, called the shamash.
They also play with a spinning top called a dreidel, and eat food fried in oil, like potato pancakes and jelly donuts!
Which would you try first? Tell me in the comments!
